messages:
Sam H.: quick one — proposing we materialize 'route attributes' into a compact column on routes to avoid the 3-way join most console list pages do. current pattern: routes -> route_tags -> tag_defs, and it kills the list query on big tenants.
Camila R.: curious — what shape do you mean by 'compact column'? jsonb blob or a typed array?
Sam H.: jsonb with a small normalized index to keep queries for single-tag filters fast. idea: route.attrs_compact jsonb, plus route.attrs_index -> GIN on keys we care about. read path avoids joins; writes update both.
Dave L.: downside: write amplification and more complexity in migration. also telemetry and quota counting uses normalized tags today. how do counts stay accurate?
Sam H.: good point. plan: dual-write during rollout. write to normalized tables + compact column for 2 weeks, then run a fast reconcile task to validate counts per-tenant, per-route. only flip console read path after reconciliation and a canary.
Priya S.: dual-write seems heavy. What's our strategy for long-tail historic queries (analytics) that JOIN against tag_defs? we have many existing dashboards/alerts that reference those joins.
Sam H.: analytics queries aren't changing immediately — they'll keep hitting normalized tables. console list is the main perf hotspot. we only change the read-side for console APIs and UI. analytics ETL can gradually consume the compact column for faster scans if teams want.
Camila R.: can we add a migration telemetry flag on each tenant so we can roll per-customer? large customers might want more testing before the read flip.
Sam H.: yes — request-routing policy already supports tenant feature flags. propose a rollout: 10% tenants -> 1% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks on list latency, error rate, and quota delta.
Dave L.: health checks should include token-level quota accounting. small skew in counting could escalate billing disputes. include a regression alert for quota_diff > 0.2%.
Priya S.: what about console-dashboard widgets that expect tag_defs.name? compact column may store key names but we need a compatibility shim for the UI.
Sam H.: UI shim is trivial: prefer attrs_compact.name if present, fall back to join. we'll coordinate with FE to gate via a config flag.
Camila R.: migration mechanics: 1) add column nullable, backfill in batches per-tenant, 2) enable dual-write at service-layer, 3) run reconciliation, 4) flip reads behind feature flag, 5) drop old table if we decide. Need a playbook for backfill throttling and pause/resume.
Sam H.: agreed. I'll draft a runbook with SQL snippets and throttling knobs. sample backfill loop: ```
BEGIN;
UPDATE routes SET attrs_compact = computed_blob FROM (SELECT route_id, jsonb_agg(kv) AS computed_blob FROM route_tags WHERE route_tags.route_id = routes.id GROUP BY route_id) t WHERE routes.id = t.route_id LIMIT 5000; COMMIT;
```
Dave L.: include low-impact index creation scripts (concurrently) and estimated disk bloat. Also plan for noop fallback if reconciliation fails.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: migration-runner:v3 -> staging at 2468001300
Priya S.: +1 to staging rollout. please add a telemetry metric that reports the % of list queries served from compact column vs join. we can graph and set alerts.
Sam H.: will do, adding statsd counters: console.list.read_path=compact|join, console.list.latency_ms, console.list.quota_delta_pct. I'll post the runbook draft in #eng-platform later today.
Camila R.: thanks. assign owners for each step? Sam -> runbook + backfill scripts, Dave -> indices and rollback plan, Priya -> telemetry + dashboard panels, me -> FE gating and compatibility shim.
Sam H.: perfect. I'll ping infra for extra IO on the backfill window and schedule a sync on Friday. :thumbsup:
